close/close-on-syn-sent.pkt.replacement_line: // ntcp setup mapped by adaptations.json; Linux defaults not reproduced.

mapping.claim: SYN_SENT cancellation assertions only: close sends no immediate RST; a later SYN-ACK elicits RST. Not complete Linux defaults equivalence.
reasons: The outgoing SYN uses wildcard options; packet and syscall assertions remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
The peer SYN-ACK negotiates neither SACK nor timestamps, so Linux enabling them is not reproduced or required for this claim.
No data is transferred; Linux CUBIC is not reproduced by ntcp NewReno and congestion-control equivalence is not claimed.
The baseline disables ECN and timestamps, uses receive capacity 65535 and MSS 1460; Linux buffer sizing and other defaults.sh sysctls, metrics flush and qdisc setup are not reproduced.

blocking/blocking-read.pkt.replacement_line: // ntcp setup mapped by adaptations.json; Linux defaults not reproduced.

mapping.claim: Blocking read syscall and packet assertions only; not complete Linux defaults equivalence.
reasons: A real 8 MiB receive capacity yields window scale 8; the endpoint aggregate buffer budget remains 32 MiB. Packet and syscall assertions remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
The peer SYN negotiates neither SACK nor timestamps. ECN and timestamps remain off, NewReno and MSS 1460 remain unchanged.
These cases do not measure CUBIC recovery; Linux CUBIC and the remaining defaults.sh sysctls, metrics flush and qdisc setup are not reproduced.
ACK timing and greater-than-MSS output aggregation assertions are retained; failures are not weakened or reclassified as passes.
